themes.title: AI trade breaks: worst week since Covid-19
themes.summary: Markets violently repriced the AI trade this week: the Nasdaq 100 entered a bear market, emerging equities followed, and Anthropic stock fell 8.5% a day after the biggest IPO ever. The trigger is fear that record AI capex - a US$7.6-trillion buildout per Economy Middle East - will not produce matching returns, and credit markets are starting to believe it.
themes.angle: The AI trade is now a returns story, not a growth story - boards should re-examine capex and vendor concentration.

themes.title: Gulf AI momentum: MGX windfall, HUMAIN, UAE kudos
themes.summary: Gulf sovereign and enterprise AI activity accelerated while global markets wobbled: Abu Dhabi's MGX booked an estimated US$20bn paper gain from Anthropic's listing, PIF-backed HUMAIN raised US$667m for Saudi AI infrastructure, and Sam Altman called the UAE the world's most forward-looking country on AI adoption. Fresh initiatives - 100,000 Arab women in AI, Dubai's Nad Zabeel campus, Sharjah's 400MW data centre - keep the regional buildout on track.
themes.angle: Gulf capital is now a direct beneficiary of - and partly hedged against - the US AI trade.

themes.title: Frontier leaps: Riemann claim, week-long agents
themes.summary: An Anthropic researcher claims Claude produced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old open problem - Bloomberg and FT both report the claim, and FT says a verified proof would be the most spectacular AI advance in mathematics. Separately, a nonprofit finds models now outperform humans at week-long tasks, and OpenAI says agents complete nearly half of 2-4 hour researcher tasks.
themes.angle: At the moment public markets question AI's ROI, frontier labs are claiming its most consequential results.

themes.title: Anthropic's public era under Wall Street scrutiny
themes.summary: Anthropic closed its record ~US$81bn IPO, opened 34% above the offer price, then slipped as the AI trade wobbled. The open question, per FT and Axios, is whether a deliberate public-benefit company can meet quarterly-capitalism expectations and reduce its dependence on constant capital infusions.
themes.angle: The first big public-market test of the benefit-company model is underway.

themes.title: Agentic AI economics heat up
themes.summary: Agentic-AI valuations keep climbing even as public AI hardware names fall: coding-agent startup Cognition is in talks at a US$75bn valuation two months after its last round, Apple is reportedly building a consumer agent to rival Meta and OpenAI, and Genesis AI raised US$500m for robot training. GlobalFoundries will test Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoids in chip fabs.
themes.angle: Money is rotating from AI infrastructure into AI-native applications.

themes.title: Regulation tightens: SEC, tariffs, EU quantum
themes.summary: Regulators and geopolitics tightened around AI: the SEC is probing Nvidia's accounting after Jensen Huang's departure (per FT), Trump threatened a 'tremendous' tax on data centres built outside the US, and Brussels plans to favour EU firms in quantum public procurement. The Neuron also flags new chip-export rules.
themes.angle: Data-centre siting is becoming a geopolitical bargaining chip - relevant to the Gulf's buildout strategy.

themes.angle: Security consolidation and local pushback mark the next phase of AI infrastructure politics.
